faqs.q: What is roof flashing and why does it leak?

runs.v: Roof flashing is the sheet metal that seals the transitions and penetrations of a roof. It leaks as the metal corrodes, wind lifts the laps, and sealant dries and cracks.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for flashing work in Belleville?

runs.v: Repairing or replacing the roof covering on a detached one- or two-family home is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and needs no construction permit, per the NJ Uniform Construction Code. Other buildings need a permit once repairs exceed 25% of the roof area in 12 months; minor flashing repairs may not need one, but confirm with the Belleville construction office first.

faqs.q: Does flashing work on a Belleville historic property need extra approval?

runs.v: A flashing repair that matches the existing metal rarely changes a building's look, but a designated landmark or a property in a historic district can need extra review, so confirm with the Belleville construction office before work starts. Per the National Park Service, a National Register listing alone places no restriction on a private owner.

faqs.q: How is step flashing installed correctly on a Belleville home?

runs.v: Step flashing uses one separate metal piece per shingle course against a sidewall or chimney, each lapping the course below so water sheds down the roof, and at a chimney it is capped by counter flashing set into the masonry. A continuous one-piece strip there is a defective installation, per InterNACHI and shingle-manufacturer guidance.

faqs.q: Does roof flashing go under shingles?

runs.v: Mostly, yes. Each step flashing piece lies under the next shingle course and open valley metal sits under the shingle edges, while apron flashing at the base of a wall or chimney laps over the top course, and counter flashing covers the vertical legs.

faqs.q: How do I fix the flashing on my roof?

runs.v: Sealant over a gap is a stopgap: a lasting fix lifts the surrounding shingles, replaces corroded or bent pieces at the correct overlaps, and reinstalls the courses. Flashing work must follow local building codes and regional weather demands, and regular maintenance with annual inspections of flashing prevents major repairs and water intrusion.
